findings.text: `ai/sessions/doc/buckets.md:26` embeds `sessions-perf/buckets-table-1920.png`, and line 30 links `sessions-perf/redraw.jsonl`. Neither file exists in the worktree or in git, so the doc shows a broken image, and its before/after redraw numbers (36–39 ms → 25–27 ms) have nothing behind them. Commit the shot and the redraw log, or drop the claims.

The grid's row count now counts the bucket rows as rows: `DataGrid.apply()` counts the `arrange()` output. The header reads about "324 of 5,810 rows" while 5,486 sessions sit inside the 5 bucket rows. Count the sessions, or label the buckets separately.

Opening a bucket (`AISessionsPage.js` `bucket_view` → `open_kinds`) puts its sessions back into the normal sorted list, scattered among the other rows instead of under the bucket row. You can't see which rows the click revealed. Nesting them under their bucket head would match how child sessions already nest.

There is a simpler way in `AISessionsPage.arrange()`: `rollup()` builds the bucket objects and the next step throws them away (`.filter(r => !r.bucket)`), then `heads` rebuilds them from `index.kind`. A plain filter (`routine.has(kind) && !open_kinds.has(kind)`) would do the same work once, and `rollup()` would stay the one place that makes bucket rows.

Sorting into buckets depends on `AISession.ix` having `agent` and `folder`. The day snapshots carry both (checked: `sessions/2026/10/12/index.json`, 708 of 708 have `folder`), but `from_index` only fills `INDEX_COLUMNS`, which has neither. A session known only from a month index has no agent name, so a cheap, short minion or mastermind run would land in "short headless" and be hidden. Check this against month loading.
The bucket rows always sit on top, whatever column header is sorted (`return [...heads, ...out]`). That is probably what you want, but it isn't written in `doc/buckets.md`.
The `Server/review.mjs:639` change (the raw-write scan also skips `ai/sessions/20…`) has nothing to do with this brief. It is harmless, in its own commit (`40cfe061c`), and the regex is right.

Scope check: this diff is a follow-on step, routine sessions rolled up into bucket rows. It does not reopen the brief's five asks, which `STATE.md` records as landed earlier (`137750706`, `fa8b19bc9`). A bucket with a null `href` draws safely in both views (`DataGridTable.js:52` and `DataGridRail.js:38` fall back to a `div`). This review had no screenshots, so it covers requirements and words only.

findings.text: The branch is out of date and will not merge. Commit 0443c3b95 (worktree/data-grid-5) conflicts with michael/dev in `ai/AISession/AISessionsPage.js` (`git merge-tree` reports CONFLICT). Since the branch was cut, the server-query parity work (d5634fab3, bf22ffdaf) moved `arrange()` into `AISessionBuckets.arrange` and made remote mode the default on the dev socket. Rebase onto michael/dev and redo the change against the new code.

Deleting `AISessionBucketView.js` breaks remote mode. On michael/dev the node query still sends bucket heads (`remote_row_of`: "A bucket head … is drawn as sent"), and `bucket_view()` (AISessionsPage.js:140) still builds an `AISessionBucketView`. Removing the file without removing those bucket heads in node (`AISessionBuckets.arrange` / the query source) leaves remote mode, which is the default, with a missing import or rows it cannot draw. Hide routine kinds in node too, or keep the file.

The chips and search only work in `?source=files` mode. The new search box and `render_kinds()` live on the files path (`render_controls`/`arrange`). Remote mode has its own `remote_controls()` search (AISessionsPage.js:~498) and never calls `arrange()`. So a chip click (`this.grid.apply(false)`) does nothing there; it needs `this.remote_ask()`, as the old bucket toggle on michael/dev does. The owner sees the remote page by default, so the asked-for "chips instead of grey rows" will not show up there.

The stats line can read "NaN routine hidden". `render_counts()` (diff, AISessionsPage.js render_counts) tests `this.filtered_count > (this.listed ?? 0)` but then subtracts `this.listed` raw. In remote mode `listed` is never set while `filtered_count` comes from the server, so the line prints `NaN`. Use the same fallback in both places, or set `listed` in `remote_ask`.
The chip head always says "routine, hidden", even when some chips are on (render_kinds). "routine:" plus the pressed state on each chip would not contradict the chips.

Search returns `{ base: hits, filtered: hits }` before the date, closed and role filters run, which is what the tooltip promises. But the role chips then total the search hits, not the window, which can surprise a reader. Worth one line in doc/buckets.md.

probe-find.mjs and find.json show it working in files mode (0 page errors at 3440/1920/400; the search reaches routine "clarity" sessions). No shot or probe covers remote mode, which is where items 2–4 break.

findings.text: In rail view, routine sessions can't be shown except by searching: sessions.css:499 now hides `.sessions-kinds`, together with the stats line that says "N routine hidden". The old bucket card was clickable in the rail. Keep the chips visible in rail view, or say in the rail that routine sessions are hidden.

The diff deletes `ai/AISession/AISessionBucketView.js`. That conflicts with the brief's "never delete" and CLAUDE.md's "never destructive" rule. Git keeps the file and files.jsonl marks it `gone`, so this is acceptable, but an archive path would follow the rule.

The tie-breaker (equal recency → costlier session first) differs between the two paths. The files path applies it to every row (AISessionRows.js:283). The node path applies it only to in-flight rows (AISessionSource.mjs:191), so two finished sessions with the same last_activity can come back in a different order in remote mode.

A search ignores the date window and the other filters on both paths (AISessionsPage.js:333 and remote_spec). That is intended and both tooltips say so. But the files path searches only the days already loaded, so a session older than the window is not found until "show 30 more days" is clicked.

files.jsonl:17–18 now lists `AISessionBucketView.js` twice: the old entry, then the appended `"gone":true` line. That is fine as an append-only log, as long as whatever reads it lets the last line win.

The shots in this diff (`sessions-perf/find-400.png`, `find-3440.png`, `find-3440-search.png`) are on the branch and not in the main tree, so I could not view them. I judged the chips from `find.json`: 5 chips, "449 sessions listed (5,640 routine hidden)", search finds server-query, no page errors.
